issues.description: The solution uses collections.deque to keep all N part positions and answers queries by indexing positions[p-1]. deque indexing is O(k) (linear in the index) in CPython, so a query asking for a large p (up to N) is O(N). With Q up to 2e5 and N up to 1e6 this yields worst-case quadratic behavior and will TLE (and practically makes the solution infeasible for large inputs).

Keeping a deque of N Python tuples (one (x,y) per part) is memory-heavy: Python tuple and int object overhead makes this approach likely to use excessive memory for N = 1e6 (risk of MLE). The data structure choice mixes the concerns of maintaining history vs. answering random-access queries; a more appropriate design is to keep only head position history in a list and compute/lookup delayed positions in O(1) time per query.

No test files or unit tests were provided alongside the implementation. Automated tests (unit or integration) covering large-N/time-limit scenarios and edge cases (e.g., p close to N, many queries of type 2) are missing.
